thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service="edge-lb" severity=critical — multiple TLS handshake failures and LB target health flapping. Alert ID: PD-984321. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-984321

PagerDuty: Escalation policy: oncall-sre -> page -> 2m repeat

Nina: acked on PagerDuty, I'm on it. Jumping into health checks + LB target groups.

Alex: seeing backend target health toggling between healthy/unhealthy in the last ~3 minutes across two AZs. Metrics: request errors 5xx spiking to ~18% on edge-prod.

Sam: any DNS changes rolled out recently? Flapping can look like targets getting traffic they can't handle if weights changed.

Nina: I just checked Route53 change history — no recent manual changes in the last 24h. Also certificate rotation job didn't run (next scheduled tomorrow).

Alex: grabbing target group describe: ```aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/edge-tg/abc123``` Got ~30% UnhealthyReason: TLSHandshakeError; backend logs show `tls: handshake failure: remote error: tls: bad record MAC` from nginx.

Sam: hmm. Could be upstream network jitter, or a client-side TLS version mismatch after a cipher downgrade. Can we confirm if this is localized to a subset of instances?

Nina: yes — instances i-0a1b2c3d and i-0f1e2d3c in us-west-2b show >60% of the failed handshakes. The rest are ~5-8%. Running a quick tcpdump on one of them now.

Maria: Support: customers reporting 502/525 and some TLS errors in browser consoles. Top impacted regions: US-WEST, small fraction in EU. No escalations yet but multiple tickets opened.

Alex: tcpdump shows many TLS ClientHello with SNI set to our domain, but server response is RST after small bytes. Kernel logs show `net: TCP: Reset due to ...` on those two instances. Could be a kernel or NIC driver issue after a recent AMI kernel patch.

Sam: good catch. Any recent host-level updates in the auto-scaling group?

Nina: ASG launched a rolling replace yesterday night with a custom AMI version v2026.02 (contains kernel 5.14.0-121). I will check the AMI bake timing vs when these nodes started flapping.

Alex: For mitigation: I recommend draining and replacing the two affected instances with older AMI and fail traffic away from them. Steps: 1) set target weight to 0 on the LB for the two instances, 2) mark out of service, 3) trigger ASG to terminate/replace.

Sam: Agreed. Also open a temporary fallback routing: shift 20% traffic to us-east-1 to reduce load on the edge region while we stabilize. Use smart-routing policy in the edge router.

Nina: executing step 1 -> setting target weight 0 now for i-0a1b2c3d and i-0f1e2d3c. ```aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn ... --attributes Key=slow_start.duration_seconds,Value=0``` (adjusting weight via internal tool).

ops-relay-bot: deploybot triggered: "replace-instance" on asg-edge-prod for i-0a1b2c3d by Nina (run id run_3772).

Nina: terminating i-0a1b2c3d -> ASG replacing. Watching health checks.

Alex: once terminated, I'll run a quick canary by re-enabling 5% traffic to new instance and monitoring TLS error rate.

Maria: telling support to message affected customers with ETA ~15-30m for mitigation. Updating incident chat in Zendesk.

Sam: routing shift to us-east-1 applied: 20% redirect in traffic policy. Monitor p50/p95 latencies and TLS error rate.

Nina: i-0a1b2c3d replaced successfully, new instance i-0d4c3b2a booted on AMI v2026.01 (older kernel). Initial health checks passing.

Alex: TLS handshake error rate dropped from 18% -> 1.6% in the affected AZ. Good sign. I'll keep one diagnostic tcpdump until we confirm stability.

Nina: terminating i-0f1e2d3c now. Ops: doing the same replacement.

ops-relay-bot: run complete: replace-instance run_3772 finished. i-0a1b2c3d replaced; i-0f1e2d3c in progress.

Maria: support updated: customers notified, no escalations requested. Monitoring open tickets for any regressions.

Sam: after both replacements, let's roll back the routing policy (remove the 20% to us-east) and re-enable normal weights. We'll keep an elevated monitoring window 60m.

Nina: i-0f1e2d3c replaced -> new i-0b9a8c7d on AMI v2026.01 and healthy. Rolling routing back now.

Alex: routing rollback done. TLS handshake rate back to baseline <0.5% globally. Edge 5xx rate back to normal.

Maria: customers notified that issue mitigated, will follow up with postmortem timeline. No data exposure reported.

Nina: handing off to Sam for the 60m watch window, then I'll prepare the incident timeline and AMI rollback recommendation for postmortem.

Sam: taking watch. I'll collect kernel logs, tcpdumps, and ASG launch history. Filing incident ticket PD-984321 with notes.

incident-bot: Incident PD-984321 acknowledged and set to mitigated. Follow-up: create postmortem, tag eng-runtime, eng-infra, and support.

Maria: thanks team. I'll draft the customer communication and coordinate final postmortem review. :thumbsup:

Nina: thanks all — great quick coordination.

Sam: watch started. I'll ping here if anything pops during the window.

ops-relay-bot: reminder scheduled in 55m to check back in and close the thread if stable."
